title: Five fixpipe requantization paths out of L0C
surface: Tensor.requant(scale=, offset=) applied to an L0C accumulator on its way to GM; the input/accumulator/destination dtype triple selecting the conversion (f16/f32 and i8/i32 into i8, u8 or f16)
study_for: The dtype triple is what selects the conversion. There is no mode enumeration in the instruction: the input dtype, the accumulator dtype and the destination dtype together decide whether this is a quantization, a requantization or a dequantization. The five cases are five triples, and the kernel derives all three dtypes from the mode name so the mapping is in one place.

The order of operations is scale, round, offset, clamp -- and the offset is after the rounding, which is observable. The reference computes `(product * scale).round() + offset` then clamps, and the odd dot products land on exact halves so ties-to-even is decided before the offset moves them anywhere. An implementation that offset first would round different lanes.

The signed and unsigned destinations are the same path with a different clamp, which is why they are two cases with one seed apart. `fp32_i8` clamps to [-128, 127] and `fp32_u8` to [0, 255], so the planted -8 column merely rounds in one and is clamped to zero in the other. Either case alone leaves the destination's signedness untested.

The scales are 0.5 and 0.25 because those are exact in the hardware's float19 parameter field. That is a deliberate restriction: an arbitrary scale would put the parameter's own packing into the comparison, and this example has no independent reference for that packing. `check_domain` refuses anything else rather than letting one in quietly.

The saturation is reached, not assumed. Rows of the first operand and columns of the second are forced to +8 and -8, and `check_domain` verifies that some scaled product actually leaves the destination's range for the integer cases. A case matrix whose clamp never fires is a clamp nobody checked.
do_not_copy_when: Your scale is not a power of two. The float19 parameter field is what carries it, and reproducing that packing independently is a separate piece of work this example does not do. A passing run here says nothing about an arbitrary scale.

You are after accumulation accuracy. Every input is a small integer, so the dot product is exact before scaling -- which is the point, because it isolates the conversion. Real FP16 accumulation error is a different question.
You are relying on the offset being applied before the rounding. It is not. Two conventions exist and this one rounds first; a requantization ported from the other convention disagrees on every tie.
